16 /-!
17 # Affine isometries
18 
19 In this file we define `AffineIsometry 𝕜 P P₂` to be an affine isometric embedding of normed
20 add-torsors `P` into `P₂` over normed `𝕜`-spaces and `AffineIsometryEquiv` to be an affine
21 isometric equivalence between `P` and `P₂`.
22 
23 We also prove basic lemmas and provide convenience constructors.  The choice of these lemmas and
24 constructors is closely modelled on those for the `LinearIsometry` and `AffineMap` theories.
25 
26 Since many elementary properties don't require `‖x‖ = 0 → x = 0` we initially set up the theory for
27 `SeminormedAddCommGroup` and specialize to `NormedAddCommGroup` only when needed.
28 
29 ## Notation
30 
31 We introduce the notation `P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂` for `AffineIsometry 𝕜 P P₂`, and `P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂` for
32 `AffineIsometryEquiv 𝕜 P P₂`.  In contrast with the notation `→ₗᵢ` for linear isometries, `≃ᵢ`
33 for isometric equivalences, etc., the "i" here is a superscript.  This is for aesthetic reasons to
34 match the superscript "a" (note that in mathlib `→ᵃ` is an affine map, since `→ₐ` has been taken by
35 algebra-homomorphisms.)
36 
37 -/
38 
39 @[expose] public section
40 
41 open Function Set Metric
42 
43 variable (𝕜 : Type*) {V V₁ V₁' V₂ V₃ V₄ : Type*} {P₁ P₁' : Type*} (P P₂ : Type*) {P₃ P₄ : Type*}
44   [NormedField 𝕜]
45   [SeminormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V] [PseudoMetricSpace P] [NormedAddTorsor V P]
46   [SeminormedAddCommGroup V₁] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V₁] [PseudoMetricSpace P₁] [NormedAddTorsor V₁ P₁]
47   [SeminormedAddCommGroup V₁'] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V₁'] [MetricSpace P₁'] [NormedAddTorsor V₁' P₁']
48   [SeminormedAddCommGroup V₂] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V₂] [PseudoMetricSpace P₂] [NormedAddTorsor V₂ P₂]
49   [SeminormedAddCommGroup V₃] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V₃] [PseudoMetricSpace P₃] [NormedAddTorsor V₃ P₃]
50   [SeminormedAddCommGroup V₄] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V₄] [PseudoMetricSpace P₄] [NormedAddTorsor V₄ P₄]
51 
52 /-- A `𝕜`-affine isometric embedding of one normed add-torsor over a normed `𝕜`-space into
53 another, denoted as `f : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂`. -/
54 structure AffineIsometry extends P →ᵃ[𝕜] P₂ where
55   norm_map : ∀ x : V, ‖linear x‖ = ‖x‖
56 
57 variable {𝕜 P P₂}
58 
59 @[inherit_doc]
60 notation:25 -- `→ᵃᵢ` would be more consistent with the linear isometry notation, but it is uglier
61 P " →ᵃⁱ[" 𝕜:25 "] " P₂:0 => AffineIsometry 𝕜 P P₂
62 
63 namespace AffineIsometry
64 
65 variable (f : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂)
66 
67 /-- The underlying linear map of an affine isometry is in fact a linear isometry. -/
68 protected def linearIsometry : V →ₗᵢ[𝕜] V₂ :=
69   { f.linear with norm_map' := f.norm_map }
70 
71 @[simp]
72 theorem linear_eq_linearIsometry : f.linear = f.linearIsometry.toLinearMap := by
73   ext
74   rfl
75 
76 instance : FunLike (P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) P P₂ where
77   coe f := f.toFun
78   coe_injective' f g := by cases f; cases g; simp
79 
80 @[simp]
81 theorem coe_toAffineMap : ⇑f.toAffineMap = f := by
82   rfl
83 
84 theorem toAffineMap_injective : Injective (toAffineMap : (P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) → P →ᵃ[𝕜] P₂) := by
85   rintro ⟨f, _⟩ ⟨g, _⟩ rfl
86   rfl
87 
88 theorem coeFn_injective : @Injective (P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) (P → P₂) (↑) :=
89   AffineMap.coeFn_injective.comp toAffineMap_injective
90 
91 @[ext]
92 theorem ext {f g : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂} (h : ∀ x, f x = g x) : f = g :=
93   coeFn_injective <| funext h
94 
95 end AffineIsometry

101 /-- Reinterpret a linear isometry as an affine isometry. -/
102 def toAffineIsometry : V →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] V₂ :=
103   { f.toLinearMap.toAffineMap with norm_map := f.norm_map }
104 
105 @[simp]
106 theorem coe_toAffineIsometry : ⇑(f.toAffineIsometry : V →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] V₂) = f :=
107   rfl
108 
109 @[simp]
110 theorem toAffineIsometry_linearIsometry : f.toAffineIsometry.linearIsometry = f := by
111   ext
112   rfl
113 
114 -- somewhat arbitrary choice of simp direction
115 @[simp]
116 theorem toAffineIsometry_toAffineMap : f.toAffineIsometry.toAffineMap = f.toLinearMap.toAffineMap :=
117   rfl

121 namespace AffineIsometry
122 
123 variable (f : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) (f₁ : P₁' →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂)
124 
125 @[simp]
126 theorem map_vadd (p : P) (v : V) : f (v +ᵥ p) = f.linearIsometry v +ᵥ f p :=
127   f.toAffineMap.map_vadd p v
128 
129 @[simp]
130 theorem map_vsub (p1 p2 : P) : f.linearIsometry (p1 -ᵥ p2) = f p1 -ᵥ f p2 :=
131   f.toAffineMap.linearMap_vsub p1 p2
132 
133 @[simp]
134 theorem dist_map (x y : P) : dist (f x) (f y) = dist x y := by
135   rw [dist_eq_norm_vsub V₂, dist_eq_norm_vsub V, ← map_vsub, f.linearIsometry.norm_map]
136 
137 @[simp]
138 theorem nndist_map (x y : P) : nndist (f x) (f y) = nndist x y := by simp [nndist_dist]
139 
140 @[simp]
141 theorem edist_map (x y : P) : edist (f x) (f y) = edist x y := by simp [edist_dist]
142 
143 protected theorem isometry : Isometry f :=
144   f.edist_map
145 
146 protected theorem injective : Injective f₁ :=
147   f₁.isometry.injective
148 
149 @[simp]
150 theorem map_eq_iff {x y : P₁'} : f₁ x = f₁ y ↔ x = y :=
151   f₁.injective.eq_iff
152 
153 theorem map_ne {x y : P₁'} (h : x ≠ y) : f₁ x ≠ f₁ y :=
154   f₁.injective.ne h
155 
156 protected theorem lipschitz : LipschitzWith 1 f :=
157   f.isometry.lipschitz
158 
159 protected theorem antilipschitz : AntilipschitzWith 1 f :=
160   f.isometry.antilipschitz
161 
162 @[continuity]
163 protected theorem continuous : Continuous f :=
164   f.isometry.continuous
165 
166 theorem ediam_image (s : Set P) : ediam (f '' s) = ediam s :=
167   f.isometry.ediam_image s
168 
169 theorem ediam_range : ediam (range f) = ediam (univ : Set P) :=
170   f.isometry.ediam_range
171 
172 theorem diam_image (s : Set P) : Metric.diam (f '' s) = Metric.diam s :=
173   f.isometry.diam_image s
174 
175 theorem diam_range : Metric.diam (range f) = Metric.diam (univ : Set P) :=
176   f.isometry.diam_range
177 
178 /-- Interpret an affine isometry as a continuous affine map. -/
179 def toContinuousAffineMap : P →ᴬ[𝕜] P₂ := { f with cont := f.continuous }
180 
181 theorem toContinuousAffineMap_injective :
182     Function.Injective (toContinuousAffineMap : _ → P →ᴬ[𝕜] P₂) := fun x _ h =>
183   coeFn_injective (congr_arg _ h : ⇑x.toContinuousAffineMap = _)
184 
185 @[simp]
186 theorem toContinuousAffineMap_inj {f g : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂} :
187     f.toContinuousAffineMap = g.toContinuousAffineMap ↔ f = g :=
188   toContinuousAffineMap_injective.eq_iff
189 
190 @[simp]
191 theorem coe_toContinuousAffineMap : ⇑f.toContinuousAffineMap = f := rfl
192 
193 @[simp]
194 theorem comp_continuous_iff {α : Type*} [TopologicalSpace α] {g : α → P} :
195     Continuous (f ∘ g) ↔ Continuous g :=
196   f.isometry.comp_continuous_iff
197 
198 /-- The identity affine isometry. -/
199 def id : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P :=
200   ⟨AffineMap.id 𝕜 P, fun _ => rfl⟩
201 
202 @[simp, norm_cast]
203 theorem coe_id : ⇑(id : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P) = _root_.id :=
204   rfl
205 
206 @[simp]
207 theorem id_apply (x : P) : (AffineIsometry.id : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P) x = x :=
208   rfl
209 
210 @[simp]
211 theorem id_toAffineMap : (id.toAffineMap : P →ᵃ[𝕜] P) = AffineMap.id 𝕜 P :=
212   rfl
213 
214 @[simp]
215 theorem toContinuousAffineMap_id : id.toContinuousAffineMap = ContinuousAffineMap.id 𝕜 P :=
216   rfl
217 
218 instance : Inhabited (P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P) :=
219   ⟨id⟩
220 
221 /-- Composition of affine isometries. -/
222 def comp (g : P₂ →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₃) (f : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₃ :=
223   ⟨g.toAffineMap.comp f.toAffineMap, fun _ => (g.norm_map _).trans (f.norm_map _)⟩
224 
225 @[simp]
226 theorem coe_comp (g : P₂ →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₃) (f : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) : ⇑(g.comp f) = g ∘ f :=
227   rfl
228 
229 @[simp]
230 theorem id_comp : (id : P₂ →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂).comp f = f :=
231   ext fun _ => rfl
232 
233 @[simp]
234 theorem comp_id : f.comp id = f :=
235   ext fun _ => rfl
236 
237 theorem comp_assoc (f : P₃ →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₄) (g : P₂ →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₃) (h : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) :
238     (f.comp g).comp h = f.comp (g.comp h) :=
239   rfl
240 
241 instance : Monoid (P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P) where
242   one := id
243   mul := comp
244   mul_assoc := comp_assoc
245   one_mul := id_comp
246   mul_one := comp_id
247 
248 @[simp]
249 theorem coe_one : ⇑(1 : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P) = _root_.id :=
250   rfl
251 
252 @[simp]
253 theorem coe_mul (f g : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P) : ⇑(f * g) = f ∘ g :=
254   rfl
255 
256 end AffineIsometry

270     s.subtypeₐᵢ.linearIsometry = s.direction.subtypeₗᵢ :=
271   rfl
272 
273 @[simp]

289 variable (𝕜 P P₂)

291 /-- An affine isometric equivalence between two normed vector spaces,
292 denoted `f : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂`. -/
293 structure AffineIsometryEquiv extends P ≃ᵃ[𝕜] P₂ where
294   norm_map : ∀ x, ‖linear x‖ = ‖x‖
295 
296 variable {𝕜 P P₂}
297 
298 -- `≃ᵃᵢ` would be more consistent with the linear isometry equiv notation, but it is uglier
299 @[inherit_doc] notation:25 P " ≃ᵃⁱ[" 𝕜:25 "] " P₂:0 => AffineIsometryEquiv 𝕜 P P₂
300 
301 namespace AffineIsometryEquiv
302 
303 variable (e : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂)
304 
305 /-- The underlying linear equiv of an affine isometry equiv is in fact a linear isometry equiv. -/
306 protected def linearIsometryEquiv : V ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] V₂ :=
307   { e.linear with norm_map' := e.norm_map }
308 
309 @[simp]
310 theorem linear_eq_linear_isometry : e.linear = e.linearIsometryEquiv.toLinearEquiv := by
311   ext
312   rfl
313 
314 instance : EquivLike (P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) P P₂ where
315   coe f := f.toFun
316   inv f := f.invFun
317   left_inv f := f.left_inv
318   right_inv f := f.right_inv
319   coe_injective' f g h _ := by
320     cases f
321     cases g
322     congr
323     simpa [DFunLike.coe_injective.eq_iff] using h
324 
325 @[simp]
326 theorem coe_mk (e : P ≃ᵃ[𝕜] P₂) (he : ∀ x, ‖e.linear x‖ = ‖x‖) : ⇑(mk e he) = e :=
327   rfl
328 
329 @[simp]
330 theorem coe_toAffineEquiv (e : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) : ⇑e.toAffineEquiv = e :=
331   rfl
332 
333 theorem toAffineEquiv_injective : Injective (toAffineEquiv : (P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) → P ≃ᵃ[𝕜] P₂)
334   | ⟨_, _⟩, ⟨_, _⟩, rfl => rfl
335 
336 @[ext]
337 theorem ext {e e' : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂} (h : ∀ x, e x = e' x) : e = e' :=
338   toAffineEquiv_injective <| AffineEquiv.ext h
339 
340 theorem coeFn_injective : @Injective (P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) (P → P₂) (fun f => f) :=
341   DFunLike.coe_injective
342 
343 /-- Reinterpret an `AffineIsometryEquiv` as an `AffineIsometry`. -/
344 def toAffineIsometry : P →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂ :=
345   ⟨e.1.toAffineMap, e.2⟩
346 
347 @[simp]
348 theorem coe_toAffineIsometry : ⇑e.toAffineIsometry = e :=
349   rfl
350 
351 /-- Construct an affine isometry equivalence by verifying the relation between the map and its
352 linear part at one base point. Namely, this function takes a map `e : P₁ → P₂`, a linear isometry
353 equivalence `e' : V₁ ≃ᵢₗ[k] V₂`, and a point `p` such that for any other point `p'` we have
354 `e p' = e' (p' -ᵥ p) +ᵥ e p`. -/
355 def mk' (e : P₁ → P₂) (e' : V₁ ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] V₂) (p : P₁) (h : ∀ p' : P₁, e p' = e' (p' -ᵥ p) +ᵥ e p) :
356     P₁ ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂ :=
357   { AffineEquiv.mk' e e'.toLinearEquiv p h with norm_map := e'.norm_map }
358 
359 @[simp]
360 theorem coe_mk' (e : P₁ → P₂) (e' : V₁ ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] V₂) (p h) : ⇑(mk' e e' p h) = e :=
361   rfl
362 
363 @[simp]
364 theorem linearIsometryEquiv_mk' (e : P₁ → P₂) (e' : V₁ ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] V₂) (p h) :
365     (mk' e e' p h).linearIsometryEquiv = e' := by
366   ext
367   rfl
368 
369 end AffineIsometryEquiv

385     e.toAffineIsometryEquiv.linearIsometryEquiv = e := by

391 theorem toAffineIsometryEquiv_toAffineEquiv :
392     e.toAffineIsometryEquiv.toAffineEquiv = e.toLinearEquiv.toAffineEquiv :=

403 namespace AffineIsometryEquiv

405 variable (e : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂)
406 
407 protected theorem isometry : Isometry e :=
408   e.toAffineIsometry.isometry
409 
410 /-- Reinterpret an `AffineIsometryEquiv` as an `IsometryEquiv`. -/
411 def toIsometryEquiv : P ≃ᵢ P₂ :=
412   ⟨e.toAffineEquiv.toEquiv, e.isometry⟩
413 
414 @[simp]
415 theorem coe_toIsometryEquiv : ⇑e.toIsometryEquiv = e :=
416   rfl
417 
418 theorem range_eq_univ (e : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) : Set.range e = Set.univ := by
419   rw [← coe_toIsometryEquiv]
420   exact IsometryEquiv.range_eq_univ _
421 
422 /-- Reinterpret an `AffineIsometryEquiv` as a `Homeomorph`. -/
423 def toHomeomorph : P ≃ₜ P₂ :=
424   e.toIsometryEquiv.toHomeomorph
425 
426 @[simp]
427 theorem coe_toHomeomorph : ⇑e.toHomeomorph = e :=
428   rfl
429 
430 protected theorem continuous : Continuous e :=
431   e.isometry.continuous
432 
433 protected theorem continuousAt {x} : ContinuousAt e x :=
434   e.continuous.continuousAt
435 
436 protected theorem continuousOn {s} : ContinuousOn e s :=
437   e.continuous.continuousOn
438 
439 protected theorem continuousWithinAt {s x} : ContinuousWithinAt e s x :=
440   e.continuous.continuousWithinAt
441 
442 /-- Interpret a `AffineIsometryEquiv` as a `ContinuousAffineEquiv`. -/
443 def toContinuousAffineEquiv : P ≃ᴬ[𝕜] P₂ :=
444   { e.toAffineEquiv, e.toHomeomorph with }
445 
446 theorem toContinuousAffineEquiv_injective :
447     Function.Injective (toContinuousAffineEquiv : _ → P ≃ᴬ[𝕜] P₂) := fun x _ h =>
448   coeFn_injective (congr_arg _ h : ⇑x.toContinuousAffineEquiv = _)
449 
450 @[simp]
451 theorem toContinuousAffineEquiv_inj {f g : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂} :
452     f.toContinuousAffineEquiv = g.toContinuousAffineEquiv ↔ f = g :=
453   toContinuousAffineEquiv_injective.eq_iff
454 
455 @[simp]
456 theorem coe_toContinuousAffineEquiv : ⇑e.toContinuousAffineEquiv = e :=
457   rfl
458 
459 /-- Reinterpret a `AffineIsometryEquiv` as a `ContinuousAffineEquiv`. -/
460 instance : Coe (P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) (P ≃ᴬ[𝕜] P₂) :=
461   ⟨fun e => e.toContinuousAffineEquiv⟩
462 
463 variable (𝕜 P)
464 
465 /-- Identity map as an `AffineIsometryEquiv`. -/
466 def refl : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P :=
467   ⟨AffineEquiv.refl 𝕜 P, fun _ => rfl⟩
468 
469 variable {𝕜 P}
470 
471 instance : Inhabited (P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P) :=
472   ⟨refl 𝕜 P⟩
473 
474 @[simp]
475 theorem coe_refl : ⇑(refl 𝕜 P) = id :=
476   rfl
477 
478 @[simp]
479 theorem toAffineEquiv_refl : (refl 𝕜 P).toAffineEquiv = AffineEquiv.refl 𝕜 P :=
480   rfl
481 
482 @[simp]
483 theorem toContinuousAffineEquiv_refl : (refl 𝕜 P).toContinuousAffineEquiv = .refl 𝕜 P := rfl
484 
485 @[simp]
486 theorem toIsometryEquiv_refl : (refl 𝕜 P).toIsometryEquiv = IsometryEquiv.refl P :=
487   rfl
488 
489 @[simp]
490 theorem toHomeomorph_refl : (refl 𝕜 P).toHomeomorph = Homeomorph.refl P :=
491   rfl
492 
493 /-- The inverse `AffineIsometryEquiv`. -/
494 def symm : P₂ ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P :=
495   { e.toAffineEquiv.symm with norm_map := e.linearIsometryEquiv.symm.norm_map }
496 
497 @[simp]
498 theorem apply_symm_apply (x : P₂) : e (e.symm x) = x :=
499   e.toAffineEquiv.apply_symm_apply x
500 
501 @[simp]
502 theorem symm_apply_apply (x : P) : e.symm (e x) = x :=
503   e.toAffineEquiv.symm_apply_apply x
504 
505 @[simp]
506 theorem symm_symm : e.symm.symm = e := rfl
507 
508 theorem symm_bijective : Bijective (AffineIsometryEquiv.symm : (P₂ ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P) → _) :=
509   Function.bijective_iff_has_inverse.mpr ⟨_, symm_symm, symm_symm⟩

543 /-- Composition of `AffineIsometryEquiv`s as an `AffineIsometryEquiv`. -/
544 def trans (e' : P₂ ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₃) : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₃ :=
545   ⟨e.toAffineEquiv.trans e'.toAffineEquiv, fun _ => (e'.norm_map _).trans (e.norm_map _)⟩
546 
547 @[simp]
548 theorem coe_trans (e₁ : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) (e₂ : P₂ ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₃) : ⇑(e₁.trans e₂) = e₂ ∘ e₁ :=
549   rfl
550 
551 @[simp]
552 theorem trans_refl : e.trans (refl 𝕜 P₂) = e :=
553   ext fun _ => rfl
554 
555 @[simp]
556 theorem refl_trans : (refl 𝕜 P).trans e = e :=
557   ext fun _ => rfl
558 
559 @[simp]
560 theorem self_trans_symm : e.trans e.symm = refl 𝕜 P :=
561   ext e.symm_apply_apply
562 
563 @[simp]
564 theorem symm_trans_self : e.symm.trans e = refl 𝕜 P₂ :=
565   ext e.apply_symm_apply
566 
567 @[simp]
568 theorem coe_symm_trans (e₁ : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) (e₂ : P₂ ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₃) :
569     ⇑(e₁.trans e₂).symm = e₁.symm ∘ e₂.symm :=
570   rfl
571 
572 theorem trans_assoc (ePP₂ : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) (eP₂G : P₂ ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₃) (eGG' : P₃ ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₄) :
573     ePP₂.trans (eP₂G.trans eGG') = (ePP₂.trans eP₂G).trans eGG' :=
574   rfl

576 /-- The group of affine isometries of a `NormedAddTorsor`, `P`. -/
577 instance instGroup : Group (P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P) where
578   mul e₁ e₂ := e₂.trans e₁
579   one := refl _ _
580   inv := symm
581   one_mul := trans_refl
582   mul_one := refl_trans
583   mul_assoc _ _ _ := trans_assoc _ _ _
584   inv_mul_cancel := self_trans_symm
585 
586 @[simp]
587 theorem coe_one : ⇑(1 : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P) = id :=
588   rfl
589 
590 @[simp]
591 theorem coe_mul (e e' : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P) : ⇑(e * e') = e ∘ e' :=
592   rfl
593 
594 @[simp]
595 theorem coe_inv (e : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P) : ⇑e⁻¹ = e.symm :=
596   rfl

598 @[simp]
599 theorem map_vadd (p : P) (v : V) : e (v +ᵥ p) = e.linearIsometryEquiv v +ᵥ e p :=
600   e.toAffineIsometry.map_vadd p v
601 
602 @[simp]
603 theorem map_vsub (p1 p2 : P) : e.linearIsometryEquiv (p1 -ᵥ p2) = e p1 -ᵥ e p2 :=
604   e.toAffineIsometry.map_vsub p1 p2

623 theorem map_eq_iff {x y : P} : e x = e y ↔ x = y :=

626 theorem map_ne {x y : P} (h : x ≠ y) : e x ≠ e y :=

629 protected theorem lipschitz : LipschitzWith 1 e :=

631

647   e.isometry.comp_continuousOn_iff

653 section Constructions
654 
655 variable (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace 𝕜 P) [Nonempty s₁] [Nonempty s₂]
656 
657 /-- The identity equivalence of an affine subspace equal to `⊤` to the whole space. -/
658 def ofTop (h : s₁ = ⊤) : s₁ ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P :=
659   { (AffineEquiv.ofEq s₁ ⊤ h).trans (AffineSubspace.topEquiv 𝕜 V P) with norm_map := fun _ ↦ rfl }
660 
661 variable {s₁}
662 
663 @[simp]
664 lemma ofTop_apply (h : s₁ = ⊤) (x : s₁) : (ofTop s₁ h x : P) = x :=
665   rfl
666 
667 @[simp]
668 lemma ofTop_symm_apply_coe (h : s₁ = ⊤) (x : P) : (ofTop s₁ h).symm x = x :=
669   rfl
670 
671 variable (s₁)
672 
673 /-- `AffineEquiv.ofEq` as an `AffineIsometryEquiv`. -/
674 def ofEq (h : s₁ = s₂) : s₁ ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] s₂ :=
675   { AffineEquiv.ofEq s₁ s₂ h with norm_map := fun _ ↦ rfl }
676 
677 variable {s₁ s₂}
678 
679 @[simp]
680 lemma coe_ofEq_apply (h : s₁ = s₂) (x : s₁) : (ofEq s₁ s₂ h x : P) = x :=
681   rfl
682 
683 @[simp]
684 lemma ofEq_symm (h : s₁ = s₂) : (ofEq s₁ s₂ h).symm = ofEq s₂ s₁ h.symm :=
685   rfl
686 
687 @[simp]
688 lemma ofEq_rfl : ofEq s₁ s₁ rfl = refl 𝕜 s₁ :=
689   rfl
690 
691 variable (𝕜) in
692 /-- The map `v ↦ v +ᵥ p` as an affine isometric equivalence between `V` and `P`. -/
693 def vaddConst (p : P) : V ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P :=
694   { AffineEquiv.vaddConst 𝕜 p with norm_map := fun _ => rfl }
695 
696 @[simp]
697 theorem coe_vaddConst (p : P) : ⇑(vaddConst 𝕜 p) = fun v => v +ᵥ p :=
698   rfl
699 
700 @[simp]
701 theorem coe_vaddConst' (p : P) : ↑(AffineEquiv.vaddConst 𝕜 p) = fun v => v +ᵥ p :=
702   rfl
703 
704 @[simp]
705 theorem coe_vaddConst_symm (p : P) : ⇑(vaddConst 𝕜 p).symm = fun p' => p' -ᵥ p :=
706   rfl
707 
708 @[simp]
709 theorem vaddConst_toAffineEquiv (p : P) :
710     (vaddConst 𝕜 p).toAffineEquiv = AffineEquiv.vaddConst 𝕜 p :=
711   rfl
712 
713 variable (𝕜) in
714 /-- `p' ↦ p -ᵥ p'` as an affine isometric equivalence. -/
715 def constVSub (p : P) : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] V :=
716   { AffineEquiv.constVSub 𝕜 p with norm_map := norm_neg }
717 
718 @[simp]
719 theorem coe_constVSub (p : P) : ⇑(constVSub 𝕜 p) = (p -ᵥ ·) :=
720   rfl
721 
722 @[simp]
723 theorem symm_constVSub (p : P) :
724     (constVSub 𝕜 p).symm =
725       (LinearIsometryEquiv.neg 𝕜).toAffineIsometryEquiv.trans (vaddConst 𝕜 p) := by
726   ext
727   rfl
728 
729 variable (𝕜 P) in
730 /-- Translation by `v` (that is, the map `p ↦ v +ᵥ p`) as an affine isometric automorphism of `P`.
731 -/
732 def constVAdd (v : V) : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P :=
733   { AffineEquiv.constVAdd 𝕜 P v with norm_map := fun _ => rfl }
734 
735 @[simp]
736 theorem coe_constVAdd (v : V) : ⇑(constVAdd 𝕜 P v : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P) = (v +ᵥ ·) :=
737   rfl
738 
739 @[simp]
740 theorem constVAdd_zero : constVAdd 𝕜 P (0 : V) = refl 𝕜 P :=
741   ext <| zero_vadd V
742 
743 include 𝕜 in
744 /-- The map `g` from `V` to `V₂` corresponding to a map `f` from `P` to `P₂`, at a base point `p`,
745 is an isometry if `f` is one. -/
746 theorem vadd_vsub {f : P → P₂} (hf : Isometry f) {p : P} {g : V → V₂}
747     (hg : ∀ v, g v = f (v +ᵥ p) -ᵥ f p) : Isometry g := by
748   convert (vaddConst 𝕜 (f p)).symm.isometry.comp (hf.comp (vaddConst 𝕜 p).isometry)
749   exact funext hg
750 
751 variable (𝕜) in
752 /-- Point reflection in `x` as an affine isometric automorphism. -/
753 def pointReflection (x : P) : P ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P :=
754   (constVSub 𝕜 x).trans (vaddConst 𝕜 x)
755 
756 theorem pointReflection_apply (x y : P) : (pointReflection 𝕜 x) y = (x -ᵥ y) +ᵥ x :=
757   rfl
758 
759 @[simp]
760 theorem pointReflection_toAffineEquiv (x : P) :
761     (pointReflection 𝕜 x).toAffineEquiv = AffineEquiv.pointReflection 𝕜 x :=
762   rfl
763 
764 @[simp]
765 theorem pointReflection_self (x : P) : pointReflection 𝕜 x x = x :=
766   AffineEquiv.pointReflection_self 𝕜 x
767 
768 theorem pointReflection_involutive (x : P) : Function.Involutive (pointReflection 𝕜 x) :=
769   Equiv.pointReflection_involutive x
770 
771 @[simp]
772 theorem pointReflection_symm (x : P) : (pointReflection 𝕜 x).symm = pointReflection 𝕜 x :=
773   toAffineEquiv_injective <| AffineEquiv.pointReflection_symm 𝕜 x
774 
775 @[simp]
776 theorem dist_pointReflection_fixed (x y : P) : dist (pointReflection 𝕜 x y) x = dist y x := by
777   rw [← (pointReflection 𝕜 x).dist_map y x, pointReflection_self]
778 
779 theorem dist_pointReflection_self' (x y : P) :
780     dist (pointReflection 𝕜 x y) y = ‖2 • (x -ᵥ y)‖ := by
781   rw [pointReflection_apply, dist_eq_norm_vsub V, vadd_vsub_assoc, two_nsmul]
782 
783 theorem dist_pointReflection_self (x y : P) :
784     dist (pointReflection 𝕜 x y) y = ‖(2 : 𝕜)‖ * dist x y := by
785   rw [dist_pointReflection_self', two_nsmul, ← two_smul 𝕜, norm_smul, ← dist_eq_norm_vsub V]
786 
787 theorem pointReflection_fixed_iff [Invertible (2 : 𝕜)] {x y : P} :
788     pointReflection 𝕜 x y = y ↔ y = x :=
789   AffineEquiv.pointReflection_fixed_iff_of_module 𝕜
790 
791 variable [NormedSpace ℝ V]
792 
793 theorem dist_pointReflection_self_real (x y : P) :
794     dist (pointReflection ℝ x y) y = 2 * dist x y := by
795   rw [dist_pointReflection_self, Real.norm_two]
796 
797 @[simp]
798 theorem pointReflection_midpoint_left (x y : P) : pointReflection ℝ (midpoint ℝ x y) x = y :=
799   AffineEquiv.pointReflection_midpoint_left x y
800 
801 @[simp]
802 theorem pointReflection_midpoint_right (x y : P) : pointReflection ℝ (midpoint ℝ x y) y = x :=
803   AffineEquiv.pointReflection_midpoint_right x y
804

809 namespace AffineSubspace
810 
811 /-- An affine subspace is isomorphic to its image under an injective affine map.
812 This is the affine version of `Submodule.equivMapOfInjective`.
813 -/
814 @[simps linear, simps! toFun]
815 noncomputable def equivMapOfInjective (E : AffineSubspace 𝕜 P₁) [Nonempty E] (φ : P₁ →ᵃ[𝕜] P₂)
816     (hφ : Function.Injective φ) : E ≃ᵃ[𝕜] E.map φ :=
817   { Equiv.Set.image _ (E : Set P₁) hφ with
818     linear :=
819       (E.direction.equivMapOfInjective φ.linear (φ.linear_injective_iff.mpr hφ)).trans
820         (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ (AffineSubspace.map_direction _ _).symm)
821     map_vadd' := fun p v => Subtype.ext <| φ.map_vadd p v }
822 
823 /-- Restricts an affine isometry to an affine isometry equivalence between a nonempty affine
824 subspace `E` and its image.
825 
826 This is an isometry version of `AffineSubspace.equivMap`, having a stronger premise and a stronger
827 conclusion.
828 -/
829 noncomputable def isometryEquivMap (φ : P₁' →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) (E : AffineSubspace 𝕜 P₁') [Nonempty E] :
830     E ≃ᵃⁱ[𝕜] E.map φ.toAffineMap :=
831   ⟨E.equivMapOfInjective φ.toAffineMap φ.injective, fun _ => φ.norm_map _⟩
832 
833 @[simp]
834 theorem isometryEquivMap.apply_symm_apply {E : AffineSubspace 𝕜 P₁'} [Nonempty E]
835     {φ : P₁' →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂} (x : E.map φ.toAffineMap) : φ ((E.isometryEquivMap φ).symm x) = x :=
836   congr_arg Subtype.val <| (E.isometryEquivMap φ).apply_symm_apply _
837 
838 @[simp]
839 theorem isometryEquivMap.coe_apply (φ : P₁' →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) (E : AffineSubspace 𝕜 P₁') [Nonempty E]
840     (g : E) : ↑(E.isometryEquivMap φ g) = φ g :=
841   rfl
842 
843 @[simp]
844 theorem isometryEquivMap.toAffineMap_eq (φ : P₁' →ᵃⁱ[𝕜] P₂) (E : AffineSubspace 𝕜 P₁')
845     [Nonempty E] :
846     (E.isometryEquivMap φ).toAffineMap = E.equivMapOfInjective φ.toAffineMap φ.injective :=
847   rfl
848 
849 end AffineSubspace
